---
title: LMArena is the only quality source today. What should the second one be?
category: ideas
fallback: general
---
Every verdict on the board rests on **LMArena Elo** from the official CC BY 4.0 dataset, with its published confidence interval. Switching the task lens re-ranks the same prices; it never blends in a second score.

That is a deliberate constraint, not a preference. A quality source is only usable here if it passes three tests:

1. **Independent.** Measured by someone other than the vendor selling the model.
2. **Redistributable.** A licence that lets a public index show the score. (Artificial Analysis fails this one: there is no redistribution licence, so its figures inform what gets checked and never what a reader sees.)
3. **Uncertain in public.** It publishes an interval, so two models it cannot separate can be declared tied instead of ranked.

Crowd preference is one kind of quality. It is not the only one a buyer cares about — agentic coding, long-context retrieval, tool-call reliability and structured output are all poorly proxied by a chat arena.

**Proposals wanted.** For any candidate, please post:

- who measures it and how often it updates;
- the licence, with a link to the licence text (not a blog post about it);
- whether it publishes uncertainty, and in what form;
- how many models on the current board it covers.

A lens that fails any of the three tests is still worth naming — say which one it fails. That list is useful to everyone building on public benchmarks.
